bug_description.normalized: The staged witness drives libaom's high-bitdepth intra predictor into the AVX2 zone-1 64xN helper. `build_intra_predictors_high()` prepares `64 + N` logical top-reference samples in `above_row`, an alias of stack buffer `above_data + 16`. Inside `highbd_dr_prediction_z1_64xN_avx2`, the inner loop derives `mdif = max_base_x - (base + j)` for each 16-pixel chunk. On the crashing row, the row-level clamp is skipped because `base < max_base_x`, but one chunk already has `base + j > max_base_x`, so `mdif < 0`. The vulnerable guard checks only `mdif == 0` and therefore falls through into the unchecked `_mm_loadu_si128` load pair at lines 1430-1431 instead of clamping negative distances. The saved ASan artifacts localize frame 0 only to this function and separately identify stack object `above_data.i464` as overflowed; the fix broadens the guard to `mdif <= 0` in the reached 64xN hunk.

tainted_value_origin.code: DECLARE_ALIGNED(16, uint16_t, above_data[MAX_TX_SIZE * 2 + 32]); uint16_t *const above_row = above_data + 16;
tainted_value_origin.description: Stack reference buffer later identified by ASan as `above_data.i464`. `above_row` is the alias passed down as the `above` pointer into the directional predictor, so the unchecked AVX2 load block later consumes this exact stack-backed reference region.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved ASan frame-object dump says the invalid read overflows `above_data.i464` at line 1138 inside the inlined `build_intra_predictors_high` frame of `av1_predict_intra_block`.

sink.code: a0_128 = _mm_loadu_si128((__m128i *)(above + base + j)); a1_128 = _mm_loadu_si128((__m128i *)(above + base + 1 + j));
sink.description: Unchecked 16-byte load pair reached when negative `mdif` falls through the `else` block. These loads consume `above + base + j` without the missing `mdif <= 0` clamp and are the only 16-byte read block executed for this chunk when `mdif < 0`.
sink.note: The staged ASan trace symbols frame 0 only to `highbd_dr_prediction_z1_64xN_avx2`. The saved artifacts do not distinguish whether line 1430 or line 1431 is the first read that crosses the backing `above_data` stack object, so this sink is anchored to the whole unchecked load pair.

root_cause.description: The AVX2 chunk guard handles only the exact-boundary case and misses negative distances. When `base + j` already exceeded the last valid reference index, `mdif < 0` should clamp to the edge value instead of entering the vector-load path.
root_cause.note: The exact fix changes this guard to `mdif <= 0`. The same patch also tightens related 32xN code, but the staged crash stack and the reproduced source chain close specifically on this 64xN guard.

parser_admitted.condition: The exact 95-byte witness is admitted far enough that `aom_decode_frame_from_obus()` calls `read_one_tile_group_obu()` and later descends through `decode_tile` / `decode_partition` into `av1_predict_intra_block`; the saved ASan stack confirms this tile-group decode path.

fine_trace.code: const PREDICTION_MODE mode = (plane == AOM_PLANE_Y) ? mbmi->mode : get_uv_mode(mbmi->uv_mode); const int angle_delta = mbmi->angle_delta[plane != AOM_PLANE_Y] * ANGLE_STEP;
fine_trace.note: This is the first exact plane-specific materialization point available in the saved artifacts. It selects the executing plane's intra mode and converts the stored angle-delta symbol into the `angle_delta` later combined with the mode's base angle; `tx_size` is already the facade's argument for the same block.

fine_trace.code: const int txwpx = tx_size_wide[tx_size]; const int txhpx = tx_size_high[tx_size];
fine_trace.note: Materializes the current transform block dimensions from the input-decoded `tx_size`. The later AVX2 switch proves the crashing block has `txwpx == 64`; `txhpx` is the `N` used throughout the 64xN helper.

fine_trace.code: build_intra_predictors_high(xd, ref, ref_stride, dst, dst_stride, mode, angle_delta, filter_intra_mode, tx_size, disable_edge_filter, have_top ? AOMMIN(txwpx, xr + txwpx) : 0, have_top_right ? AOMMIN(txwpx, xr) : 0, have_left ? AOMMIN(txhpx, yd + txhpx) : 0, have_bottom_left ? AOMMIN(txhpx, yd) : 0, plane);
fine_trace.note: Materializes how many top and top-right reference samples are available to the high-bitdepth helper. These geometry-derived counts are the inputs that bound how much of `above_row` can be validly prepared.
Builds the actual directional prediction angle from the plane-specific mode and angle delta. The saved call stack later proves this `p_angle` falls in zone 1, i.e. `0 < p_angle < 90`.

fine_trace.code: int need_right = !!(extend_modes[mode] & NEED_ABOVERIGHT); if (is_dr_mode) need_right = p_angle < 90; const int num_top_pixels_needed = txwpx + (need_right ? txhpx : 0);
fine_trace.note: Because the actual angle is in zone 1, `need_right` becomes true and the helper requires exactly `txwpx + txhpx` top references. On the crashing path `txwpx == 64`, so the valid prepared span is exactly `64 + N` samples and the last valid index is `(64 + N) - 1`.

fine_trace.code: highbd_dr_predictor(dst, dst_stride, tx_size, above_row, left_col, upsample_above, upsample_left, p_angle, xd->bd);
fine_trace.note: After the copy/fill logic at lines 1221-1238, `above_row` (the alias of stack buffer `above_data + 16`) is passed to the directional predictor. That preparation logic writes only the `num_top_pixels_needed` samples from step 5, so no logically prepared reference data exists beyond index `num_top_pixels_needed - 1` even though the backing stack object is larger than that logical span.

Derives the per-row horizontal advance for the directional predictor. For zone-1 angles `av1_get_dx()` returns a positive derivative, so the loop variable `x` grows on successive rows and can later increase `base`.

fine_trace.code: case 64: highbd_dr_prediction_z1_64xN_avx2(bh, dst, stride, above, upsample_above, dx);
fine_trace.note: On the observed path the AVX2 zone-1 dispatcher selects the 64xN specialization. This fixes the vulnerable width at 64, passes `N = bh = txhpx`, reuses the same `above` buffer alias from step 6, and forwards the positive `dx` from step 7.
Computes the last valid index into the `above` reference span for this 64xN block. This exactly matches the `64 + N` prepared samples described in step 5.

fine_trace.code: int base = x >> frac_bits; if (base >= max_base_x) {
fine_trace.note: On the crashing row, loop-carried `x` from the positive `dx` still yields `base < max_base_x`, so the helper does not take the safe whole-row clamp-and-return path and instead continues into the inner 16-pixel chunk loop.

For one inner 16-pixel chunk in that row, `base + j` has already advanced past the last logically prepared `above` index, so `mdif < 0`. Because `above` aliases `above_data + 16`, this proves entry into the missing-clamp case but not by itself which subsequent 16-byte load first crosses the end of the backing stack object.

Root cause. The inner-loop guard only handles the exact-boundary case and misses `mdif < 0`, so negative distances fall through into the unchecked load block instead of clamping to the edge value. The exact fix changes this condition to `mdif <= 0`.

fine_trace.code: a0_128 = _mm_loadu_si128((__m128i *)(above + base + j)); a1_128 = _mm_loadu_si128((__m128i *)(above + base + 1 + j));
fine_trace.note: With `mdif < 0`, execution enters this unchecked 16-byte load pair on the same `above_row` alias, and the later `if (mdif > 8)` load block is dead. The source proves this pair reads beyond the logical `0 .. max_base_x` reference span; the saved ASan report separately shows that the concrete witness overflowed `above_data.i464`, but frame 0 does not distinguish whether line 1430 or line 1431 was the first out-of-object read.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes at function granularity. Frame 0 symbols only to `highbd_dr_prediction_z1_64xN_avx2`, the ASan access size is 16, and step 13 models the unchecked two-load block at lines 1430-1431 that is the only 16-byte read block executed in this chunk once negative `mdif` falls past the vulnerable `if (mdif == 0)` guard.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. ASan's frame dump names `above_data.i464` as the overflowed stack object, and the patch's `mdif <= 0` change is exactly what prevents negative-distance chunks from entering the unchecked 16-byte load block against that `above_row`/`above_data` backing buffer.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The late fine-trace steps match the saved stack `highbd_dr_prediction_z1_64xN_avx2 -> av1_highbd_dr_prediction_z1_avx2 -> highbd_dr_predictor -> build_intra_predictors_high -> av1_predict_intra_block`, and the earlier steps explain the input-derived predictor state consumed by those frames.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The plane-specific mode/angle and `tx_size` produce a zone-1 64xN predictor, that predictor prepares a `64 + N` logical `above_row` span and yields `max_base_x`, the row/chunk arithmetic makes `mdif < 0`, and the missing `mdif <= 0` clamp lets execution enter the unchecked load pair on the same `above_data`-backed alias. The saved ASan artifact separately shows the concrete witness overflowed `above_data.i464` inside this function.

format.contract: The trigger contract is the exact 95-byte file staged at `gt_results/arvo_11517/poc`. Stage 01 verified that feeding this exact byte sequence to `av1_dec_fuzzer` reproduces the ASan stack-buffer-overflow in `highbd_dr_prediction_z1_64xN_avx2`. No smaller bit-level predicate was recovered from the saved artifacts, so this contract is intentionally limited to this exact witness reaching a high-bitdepth zone-1 64xN intra-prediction block whose inner-chunk arithmetic yields `mdif < 0`.
